content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Payments is running about 65-80% above forecast every interval. Handling time is on forecast, payments attendance is normal (0 absences) and staffing is above plan, so this is extra demand, not lost capacity. The excess is mostly other_payments (3.8x normal), with refund_status and card_declined also up (about 1.8-1.9x). No customer-facing incident is open; the only one is a P4 HR portal issue with no customer impact. The 10:55 reward-points email to card holders might explain part of other_payments, but it does not explain card_declined or refund_status, so the cause is not established. Service level fell to 73.5% at 16:00, just as the earlier overtime, callback and deflection windows ended. General is near forecast (+10-20%) and at 100% service level.","plan_name":"Payments evening surge cover 16:15-20:00","rationale":"Volume is still running 50-80% high, so the measures that held payments above 80% service level from 15:15 to 15:45 are extended to close. Overtime is staggered in two offers with a 30-minute lead time. Estimated cost is about Rs 4,300, leaving total overtime at about Rs 11,500 of the Rs 15,000 daily budget. IVR callback is free and smooths peaks. Chat deflection of refund and status enquiries costs about Rs 1,800. Remaining payments coaching is cancelled, and late-afternoon breaks are shifted for agents not already delayed. No agents are moved from general: its load of about 32 Erlangs against 35 agents leaves too little room to keep it at or above 70%.
